context: A boss mentors a uni intern
purpose: Teach: 独創/船舶/専務/チェックイン/資する/格別/見返り/退任

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.en: Ren, originality is the lifeblood of any company.
lines.style: Measured, purposeful opening. Not lecturing—instructing with the weight of experience. Slight pause after the name, letting it land. Steady eye contact. The tone of someone who has built something and knows what it takes.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。船舶業界、規模感、勉強になります。
lines.en: Yes. The scale of the shipping industry—I'm learning so much from it.
lines.style: Genuine deference without self-diminishment. The first 'yes' is quick, respectful. Then he leans into his own thought on 'scale'—quieter, more reflective. A young person actually thinking, not performing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 専務との面会、勉強の機会だ。
lines.en: Your meeting with the executive vice president—that's where you'll really learn.
lines.style: Lean forward slightly on 'executive vice president.' Not a directive so much as a highlight. Quiet conviction that this moment matters. The specific responsibility of someone being entrusted.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 海外チェックインの慣習、現場で学びます。
lines.en: I'll learn the customs of international operations firsthand, out in the field.
lines.style: Soft but steady. Not defensive about being young or inexperienced. The phrase 'firsthand, out in the field' carries a note of resolution—he's committing to the work, not just the idea.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: CSR活動、社会に資する形で。
lines.en: CSR work—the kind that actually serves society, not just the company.
lines.style: Slight tonal shift toward gravity. The dash gives weight to the clarification. Not cynical, but clear-eyed about what matters. The pause before 'not just the company' carries quiet conviction.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 格別なご縁、見返りなく、続けたいです。
lines.en: These ties mean a lot to me—I want to continue them, not because I'm obligated, but because they matter.
lines.style: Vulnerable opening. The word 'mean' carries genuine warmth. Then he corrects himself slightly—'not because I'm obligated'—checking himself, being precise about why he cares. Earnest without being effusive.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 退任後の人生設計も、若いうちから考えろ。
lines.en: Start thinking about your life after you step back from this role—even now, while you're young.
lines.style: Quieter, more reflective. Not a warning, but wisdom settling in. The rhythm slows on 'even now, while you're young.' A grandfather-like quality—the kind of counsel that assumes he'll be around to see how it unfolds.
